title: Electrons through two slits: waves against particles
caption: If electrons were classical particles the two slits would give the sum P₁ + P₂ (dashed): a smooth hump. Adding amplitudes, P = |ψ₁ + ψ₂|² = |ψ₁|² + |ψ₂|² + interference terms, gives fringes (solid) spaced by λD/d = 5.4 pm × 1 m/1 μm = 5.4 μm, with zero at the dark fringes and twice the classical value at the bright ones.
alt: Graph of probability against position on the screen from -14 to 14 micrometres: a smooth dashed hump for classical particles and a solid fringe pattern oscillating between zero and twice that hump with period 5.4 micrometres.
description: The horizontal axis is position on the screen in micrometres; the vertical axis is the probability density in arbitrary units.
The dashed curve is P₁ + P₂, the classical sum for particles passing through one slit or the other: no fringes.
The solid curve is P = P₁ + P₂ + interference term: bright fringes where the paths differ by a whole number of wavelengths, spaced by x = λD/d = 5.4 μm.
At the centre the fringe peak is twice the classical value; halfway between fringes (2.7 μm) the probability falls to zero.
